dialogReference.para: The digital elevation model raster to convert. Must be a single-band raster containing elevation values. Both floating-point and integer pixel types are supported; NoData cells are handled automatically based on the chosen Model Footprint.

pythonReference.para: Path or layer reference to the input single-band elevation raster.

dialogReference.para: The vertical unit of measure for the elevation values stored in the DEM (Meters or Feet).

When the DEM's spatial reference includes a Vertical Coordinate System (VCS), this value is auto-detected and pre-populated when the DEM is selected. Many DEMs lack a formal VCS even when the elevation unit is well-known; in those cases the field is left blank and a warning is shown - manual selection is required.

Choosing the wrong unit when elevation and horizontal (XY) units differ will produce a model with unintended vertical exaggeration. For example, treating feet as meters introduces an approximately 3.28x vertical stretch at Vertical Exaggeration = 1.0.

pythonReference.para: "Meters" or "Feet". The vertical unit of the elevation values in the DEM.

dialogReference.para: Path and filename for the output binary STL file. If the .stl extension is omitted it is added automatically. The file is compatible with any 3D printing slicer software.

pythonReference.para: Full output file path. The .stl extension is appended if omitted.

dialogReference.para: The longest dimension of the 3D printer's build plate in millimeters. The model is uniformly scaled so its longest horizontal axis equals this value. The other horizontal axis scales proportionally.
Typical values: 100–220 mm for desktop FDM printers; up to 350 mm for large-format machines. Default: 180 mm.

pythonReference.para: Maximum build-plate dimension in millimeters (must be > 0). The model's longest horizontal axis is scaled to fit this value.

dialogReference.para: Multiplier applied to terrain relief after all unit conversions. Use 1.0 for a true-scale representation. Values greater than 1.0 amplify topographic relief, which is useful for relatively flat terrain where the natural relief would be too subtle to see at the chosen scale. Base thickness is not affected. Default: 1.0.

pythonReference.para: Vertical exaggeration multiplier (must be > 0). 1.0 produces a geometrically accurate model.

dialogReference.para: The smallest surface feature to preserve in the output model, in millimeters. Before triangulation the DEM is resampled to a cell size that yields this feature size at the chosen scale. The cell size is never made finer than the DEM's native resolution (no upsampling).
Smaller values capture finer terrain detail but produce more triangles and larger files. A value of 0.2–0.5 mm is a practical range for most FDM printers. Default: 0.2 mm.

pythonReference.para: Smallest resolvable feature in the output model, in millimeters (must be > 0). Controls the resampling resolution before triangulation.

dialogReference.para: Thickness of the solid flat base beneath the lowest terrain elevation, in millimeters. A minimum of 1–2 mm is recommended to prevent warping or tipping during printing. Set to 0 to omit the base (not recommended for most printers). Default: 3.0 mm.

pythonReference.para: Solid base thickness in millimeters (must be ≥ 0).

dialogReference.para: Controls which elevation is mapped to the bottom of the terrain surface (the top of the base layer).

bulletList.bullet_item: Sea Level (0) - Elevation 0 is the terrain floor. Terrain at or below sea level still appears in the model; the lowest value present sets the actual print-plate contact surface. Useful when the datum relationship matters, such as a coastal area that includes bathymetry.
Minimum Elevation - The lowest elevation in the DEM is mapped to the terrain floor. The full base thickness sits directly beneath the lowest terrain point, maximising the visible relief of the model.

dialogReference.para: Controls how NoData cells at the DEM boundary are handled.

bulletList.bullet_item: Tight (Follows DEM Boundary) - NoData cells are left as void. Perimeter walls follow the actual data boundary of the DEM, producing a smaller, more printable model when the survey area is not rectangular.
Rectangular - NoData cells are filled with the floor elevation, producing a flat-based rectangular block with four straight perimeter walls.

summary.para: Converts a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) raster to a watertight binary STL file suitable for 3D printing. The model is scaled so its longest horizontal axis fills the specified print-bed dimension, with configurable vertical exaggeration, mesh density, and base thickness.

usage.para: The DEM is resampled to a resolution controlled by Minimum Detail Size before triangulation, so triangle count is appropriate for the chosen print scale regardless of the DEM's native resolution. The output mesh is fully watertight: terrain surface, perimeter walls, and flat bottom are all closed with consistent outward-facing normals.

If the DEM stores elevation in different units from its horizontal coordinate system - for example, UTM meters (XY) with NAVD 88 feet (Z) - set Elevation Units to the correct vertical unit. The tool applies the necessary conversion factor automatically, so the model has correct proportions at Vertical Exaggeration = 1.0.

dataIdInfo.idAbs: Converts a DEM raster to a watertight binary STL file for 3D printing.
